en.html:
Since morning the sky had looked untrustworthy. Near noon it stopped pretending. Heavy drops battered the garden soil, determined that all the careful daily maintenance should come to precisely nothing.

Thunder also was making its presence known. Still distant, but apparently coming nearer. The weather had more complaints to deliver.

en.html:
All that heavenly noise, and no substance. It could not stop my thoughts sinking into their usual darkness. Nobody to talk to, either.

The Chief was at work. Makimura, the steward, was busy. Muramasa had gone on her daily search for the Silver Star. Rain interfered with a tsurugi's sensors, but apparently her ability to catch the Silver Star's presence was a separate matter. That department worked.

Rust was not a concern for her. Rain probably caused no difficulty either. I pictured my spider-shaped partner flying through dark Kamakura, shedding droplets, and envied her. Some work in hand, and the mind need not sit unemployed with its misery.

...I had fought.
Fought, fought, and killed.

Many warriors infected by the Silver Star's eggs had fallen to me. Exactly as many people who stood beside me, I had killed afterward.

Good and evil cancel each other out.

The rule of slaughter imposed on me was not finished. More killing remained.

Who next? Who would be enemy, who ally? Both, in the end, to be cut down.

The enemy, I did not know. The Silver Star, or whoever carried the last egg.
The ally—the ally, I knew.

天の喧騒はしかし、どこか空虚で、憂鬱な思索へと
沈みたがる意識を引き止める役には立たなかった。
　話し相手になってくれる人もいない。

　署長は出勤中、<ruby>家宰<rt>かさい</rt></ruby>の牧村さんは繁忙である。
　村正も日課の銀星号捜索に出向いていていない。雨
は劒冑の探査機能を妨害するが、銀星号の<ruby>香気<rt>けはい</rt></ruby>を掴む
能力はまた別なので問題ないようだ。

　錆びを知らぬ劒冑は雨中の探索行も苦としないのだ
ろう。水滴を弾きながら暗い鎌倉を飛び回る蜘蛛の姿
の相棒を思って、俺は羨んだ。
　為すべき何事かがあれば、無為に悩まなくても済む。

　……戦ってきた。
　戦って、戦って、殺してきた。

　銀星号の〝卵〟に冒された武者を幾人となく斃した。
　そして同じ数だけ、俺の傍らにいたひとを殺した。

　善悪相殺。

　俺に課せられたこの<ruby>虐殺法<rt>ルール</rt></ruby>は、まだ終わりを迎えて
いない。
　まだ、殺さなくてはいけない。

　次は誰を殺すのか。
　誰を敵とし、誰を味方とし、その両方を斬り伏せる
のか。

　敵はわからない。銀星号か、それとも最後の〝卵〟
預けられた誰かか。
　味方は――味方は、わかっている。

en.html:
Her, probably.
The girl who went forward, single-mindedly searching for the right path.

I admired that. Envied it. Every meeting, every sight of her, added to the feeling.

Had it been permitted, I too would have wanted to live like that.

Seedha chalo. Walk straight. Such a small instruction, and she could actually do it. Not spend the whole journey explaining why today's crookedness was compulsory, tomorrow's would be regrettable, and after that surely the straight road would begin.

Rightly.
Straight ahead.
Without swerving—

For me, that road was closed. So many sins, so many mistakes. Bound to them, responsible for them: that was the life still available to me. My admiration did not reopen any road. It merely stood at the closed one, looking through.

Ichijou Ayane was far away, and precious to me.

Therefore, I would probably kill her.

Haan. Such was the excellent destination of my feelings.

When I killed the next enemy.
Her—

en.html:
For one instant I thought my gloomy mind had started manufacturing ghosts. No. The girl was real.

She stood there. Not moving.
No words. No expression.

A welcome visitor, certainly. Yet calling out to her did not seem so simple. That fiercely straight-ahead gaze of hers had disappeared. A misty blankness had taken its place. Stone Buddha eyes.

A lifeless statue is carved out of somebody's entire passion. Likewise, behind her still eyes, a storm was plainly there. What kind, I could not make out.

I had never seen this Ichijou. Not even when we first met and she openly loathed me. And she looked at me as if I too were appearing before her for the first time.

Cold. Nothing to do with the rain or the season. Some other thing was freezing me.

Fear, perhaps.

—Of what? What exactly was I afraid of?

In the icy rain she silently thrust out an arm. Like pointing a gun.

A scrap of paper was gripped in her hand.

陰鬱な思索が幻を呼んだのかと、刹那はそう考えた。
　――違う。少女は実在だ。

　少女はそこにいて、そこに立ち尽くしている。

　物も言わない。
　表情もない。

　俺にすれば、歓迎すべき来客だ。
　しかし、声を掛けるのが躊躇われた。

　彼女特有の、苛烈なまでに真っ直ぐ前方へと向けら
れる眼光が、今は影を潜め、どこか靄のかかったそれ
に取って代わられている。
　その平板な瞳が石仏を思わせた。

　無機質なる仏像がその実、彫師の情念の丈をもって
打ち上げられているのと同じく、少女の揺れぬ双眸の
奥にも波濤があるのは容易に窺える。
　だが、その実相が見えない。

　初めて目にする一条だった。出会って最初の頃の、
俺を露骨に嫌悪していた姿とも違う。
　そして彼女もまた、初めて見るかのような目を俺に
向けているのだった。

　肌寒い。
　雨とも季節柄とも関わりなく、何かに凍える。

　それは恐れであったのかもしれない。
　
　――何を？　何を恐れるのか？

　氷雨に打たれる少女は音もなく、片腕を突き出した。
　それは銃を突きつける挙措に似ていた。

　手の中に、紙切れを握っている。

With Ichijou, I went to a cinema in Kita-Kamakura. Almost empty, probably on account of the weather. For roughly two hours we watched what appeared to be watermelon and rubber boots boiled together in glue. This preparation was being offered as a film.

What to feel about it, neither clarity nor instructions were available. We went to a nearby soba shop for a late lunch. Now we sat across a table.

Why she had invited me so suddenly, I had not asked. Curiosity was there, but the occasion kept passing without the question coming out.

Partly, I was grateful to be rescued from brooding alone. More than that, something was wrong with Ichijou today. An atmosphere surrounded her which did not encourage casual inquiries.

Even now, it remained.

一条と連れ立って、北鎌倉の銀幕へ入り。
　天候のせいだろう、閑散としていた館内で二時間程、
スイカと長靴を接着剤で煮込んだような内容の映画を
鑑賞し。

　何とも曖昧な感慨に浸りつつ、遅い昼食をとるため
近場の蕎麦屋へ。
　今はその卓の一つで向かい合っている。

　一条の唐突な誘いにどんな意図があったのか、それ
はまだ訊いていない。
　関心はあったが、訊きそびれた。

　何であれ陰鬱な孤独からの救いは有難かったという
のも理由ではある。がそれ以上に、やはり今日の一条
はどこかおかしく、安直な問いかけを躊躇わせる空気
に包まれているのが大きかった。

　この時点においてもそうだ。

Soba Shop Girl 2"Haan ji, your order?"
Kageaki"Ichijou, what will you take?"
Ichijou"Ah, yes. Um... still serving chilled tanuki?"
Soba Shop Girl 2"Still? Madam, this establishment has never served crimes against humanity."
Ichijou"...Ek minute. What crime against humanity?"
Soba Shop Girl 2"Ji?"
Kageaki"Ichijou, what are you saying?"
Ichijou"What... what?"
Kageaki"Tempura crumbs, soaked in cold soup, then eaten. At what point was humanity given permission for this? Go back to Australopithecus also. Absolutely not."
Soba Shop Girl 2"Exactly. Your companion is very good at jokes."
Kageaki"Yes. This side of her is news to me also."
Ichijou"...Um..."
Soba Shop Girl 2"Actually, I heard a strange rumor. Some shop is really preparing this chilled tanuki and serving it to customers, apparently..."
Kageaki"Impossible. Urban legend. Or some sort of bluff—a MacGuffin, perhaps."
Kageaki"One joker describes it as real. The listener cooperates by pretending to believe. The exchange is amusing, so it catches on. That must be the business, no?"
Soba Shop Girl 2"Haan, wohi toh! Exactly what I thought. I know, of course I know..."
Kageaki"You also enjoy a joke, I see."
Soba Shop Girl 2"Ahahaha!"
Ichijou"…………"

蕎麦屋の娘２「お客さん、ご注文は？」
景明「一条、どうする」
一条「あ、はい。 　えーっと……冷やしたぬきまだやってる？」
蕎麦屋の娘２「まだも何も、そのような反人類的な代物を うちの店では出してません」
一条「……いやちょっと待て。 　反人類的って何だ」
蕎麦屋の娘２「はい？」
景明「何を言っているんだ一条」
一条「え……え？」
景明「天かすを冷たい汁につけて食う・・・・・・・・・・・・・・などという 行為が人類に許されている筈もないだろう。 　アウストラロピテクスまで遡っても断じて 有り得ないぞ」
蕎麦屋の娘２「ええ、まったく。 　今日のお連れさんは冗談がお上手で」
景明「は、自分も意外な一面を見た思いです」
一条「……えーと……」
蕎麦屋の娘２「そういえば最近、変な噂を聞きましたよ。 　その冷やしたぬきとかいうやつを、本当に 作って客に出している店があるとか……」
景明「まさか。都市伝説でしょう。 　いや、はったり表現マクガフィンの一種かもしれません」
景明「どこかの冗談好きがあたかも実在のものの ように語り、聞いた相手も調子を合わせて真 に受けてみせる。そのやり取りが面白いので 流行した……そんなところではありませんか」
蕎麦屋の娘２「ですよね？　やっぱそうですよねー。 　やっ、わかってるんですけどね」
景明「貴方も冗談がお好きなようだ」
蕎麦屋の娘２「あっはっはっ」
一条「…………」
景明「それで一条。 　冗談はさておき、注文をどうする」
一条「は、はぁ。 　じゃあ……普通のたぬきで……」
景明「そうか。良いところを選んだな。 　では、自分も同じものを」
蕎麦屋の娘２「はい、たぬき二つ！」

Kageaki"Our graduation trip. My friends and I toured Kamakura's famous places."
Kageaki"Visited the Five Mountains, played at assassinating Sanetomo in Hachimangu... Then lunchtime arrived, so we entered a nearby soba shop. This one."
Kageaki"One mistake I had made on that trip. Insufficient money."
Kageaki"The others had brought extra pocket money for the occasion. One expensive order after another, as if to taunt me. No, remove the 'as if.' Taunting me was the purpose."
Kageaki"Even now I remember. Konagaya ordered soba with grated yam and radish. Ozaki, the same. Andou, I believe, took a large special soba."
Kageaki"Every item above one hundred yen. My entire financial strength was a hundred and some change. They knew this very well."
Kageaki"You understand?"
Ichijou"…………N-no, I don't."

景明「実はその旅行で、俺は失敗を犯していた。 　手持ちの金が少なかったのだ」
景明「皆は違った。せっかくの旅行なのだからと、 多めに小遣いを持ってきていた。 　彼らはあてつけの如く、というかあてつけ だったのだが、次々と高い品を注文した」
景明「今でも覚えている。 　小長谷こながやは山かけおろし蕎麦だった。尾崎も 同じだ。安藤はたしか、特選蕎麦の大盛りを 頼んでいたと思う」

en.html:
Ichijou(What am I being asked to understand...?)
Kageaki"A challenge. Himmat hai? Spend your entire fortune here and preserve your pride. Have you that greatness in you?"
Kageaki"Their superior smiles settled my decision. One hundred twenty-five yen in the wallet. I checked. Once the figure was confirmed, hesitation was finished."
Kageaki"Tanuki soba. Sixty yen. I placed the order."
Ichijou(...Himmat nahin thi. So the greatness was NOT there.)
Kageaki"Their noodles arrived. They began eating with great satisfaction, offering me surface-level pity while I waited for mine."
Kageaki"When it came to humiliating a defeated man, complete experts."
Ichijou"These people were your friends? Really?"
Kageaki"But little did they know: victory and defeat were shortly to exchange seats."
Kageaki"The turning point was the arrival of my soba."
Kageaki"One look was sufficient. Everybody could see the reversal."
Kageaki"Outside, Konagaya muttered, 'The saala ordered the cheapest thing and ate the best thing.' Beside him, Ozaki was desperately memorizing the shop's location."
Kageaki"The winner was myself."
Ichijou"…………. So, um... in the end, what was the soba actually like?"
Kageaki"Yes. Such was the matter."
Ichijou"What?"
Soba Shop Girl 2"Here you are!"

一条（何を訊かれてるのかが……）
景明「彼らは挑戦していた。 　この場で全財産をはたき、プライドを守る だけの度量が、貴様にあるのかと」
景明「彼らの優越感に満ちた笑みは、俺に一つの 決断をさせるに充分だった。 　財布の中身は一二五円。それさえ確認すれ ば、もう迷いなどなかった」
景明「俺はたぬき蕎麦を注文した。 　六〇円だった」
一条（……無かったんだ。度量……）
景明「彼らは注文の蕎麦が届くと、実に旨そうに 食べ始めた。 　たぬき蕎麦を待つ俺に、上辺だけの憐れみ の言葉を掛けながらだ」
景明「敗者を貶める事にかけて彼らは達人だった」
一条「本当に仲間だったんですか？　その人たち」
景明「しかし、彼らは知らなかったろう。 　勝敗がわずかな時間で覆る運命にあったと は」
景明「その転機は、俺の蕎麦が来た瞬間に訪れた」
景明「一目でわかった。 　すべてが逆転したことは誰の目にも明らか だった」
景明「店を出た時、小長谷が呟いた。一番安いの 頼んだやつが一番旨いもの食いやがった、と。 　その横で尾崎は店の場所を必死に覚えよう としていた」
景明「俺は勝者だった」
一条「…………。 　それで、あのー。結局、どんな蕎麦だった んです？」
景明「うむ。 　そういうものだ」
一条「はい？」
蕎麦屋の娘２「あいよ、お待ちー！」

The tempura crumbs crackled and danced in the broth. Only here had I eaten tanuki soba whose topping was so energetically alive. Making crumbs pop sounded simple enough. Making the taste cooperate might be the difficulty. Here, the lively crumbs and the noodles were in perfect agreement.

Ichijou looked satisfied too.

If this got her talking a little more, that would be good.

What came next, who could say? The recent upheaval had given political stability a firm push in the opposite direction. Its long-term effects were a separate question.

Take the gloomy view, and this shop might close again before the returning customers arrived.
